title: Analysis of the Influence of the Exposome in Patients With Non-communicable Diseases
official: Analysis of the Influence of the Exposome in Patients With Non-communicable Diseases: a Cross-sectional Study
summary: It is well documented that factors such as obesity, a sedentary lifestyle, and comorbidities-including hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia-increase the risk of developing non-communicable diseases (NCDs). However, few studies have evaluated the influence of the exposome, which encompasses both internal and external factors. While existing literature examines isolated factors, research integrating both dimensions remains scarce. Assessing exposome components enables a better understanding of the complex interplay between the environment, lifestyle, and health status. This study aims to provide mechanistic insight into the impact of exposomic factors-such as climatic variations, lifestyle behaviors, and pollution-on NCDs.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patient (male or female) aged 40 or older.
* Patient receiving outpatient or inpatient care at RAMSAY SANTE hospitals.
* Patient who has been informed and has not objected.
* Patient affiliated with or a beneficiary of a social security scheme.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patient lacking the intellectual or physical capacity to provide consent.
* Pregnant, breastfeeding, or recently delivered woman.
* Patient subject to legal protection measures (guardianship, trusteeship, etc.) or deprived of liberty by judicial or administrative decision.
